paragraphs: The controller validates a positive decimal amount and a client request key. It resolves account ownership from the authenticated session; it never accepts another customer's account merely because its ID is supplied.

The service loads the persisted request under a row lock. Its saved account_id and amount are authoritative. If a previous delivery already completed, return that result. Next lock the account, check ACTIVE and current funds, and perform a guarded debit.

Insert a uniquely referenced ledger entry and an audit event in the same transaction. Commit before acknowledging success. A duplicate-key or database exception rolls back the debit; it does not leave money removed without a ledger record.

Atomicity applies to the writes enclosed by one BEGIN/COMMIT. Consistency means the amount, status, ledger/allocation and audit invariants agree. Isolation prevents conflicting decisions on locked rows. Durability means a committed result survives a client disconnect.

On unexpected database errors, roll back the local transaction. A known business rejection can instead be recorded and committed without a financial mutation. Never swallow a database exception and accidentally commit half of the intended changes.
All balance mutations here belong to the same local database transaction. External notifications are deferred until after commit; adding an external transfer changes the atomicity boundary.

SQL fragments show the successful branch of an application-controlled transaction. Comments describing checks are real control-flow requirements: the handler must stop/rollback or record the specified exception when a guard fails. Do not paste all branches as one unconditional money-moving script.

paragraphs: A waiting worker must re-read the row after it obtains the lock. A value read before waiting cannot authorize a later debit/allocation. A second delivery of one business request differs from a genuinely new request: the former returns the same outcome, while the latter must recheck current funds or remaining obligation.

SELECT ... FOR UPDATE is a locking read inside an explicit InnoDB transaction. The row remains protected until COMMIT or ROLLBACK. Use indexed primary/unique lookups so the operation does not scan and lock unrelated data.

Every handler touching multiple entities must follow the same lock hierarchy. Define it once for workers, callbacks and reconcilers; opposite order can create deadlocks. A deadlock victim must restart the whole local transaction and re-read data.
Lock the saved business request/payment first, then its mutable account/invoice/item. Keep the transaction short and use current locked values, even if an earlier page showed a different balance.

Amounts shown in tables use two decimal places; commas and ₹ are display formatting, not database values. Round according to the documented currency/payroll rule once at the defined boundary. Do not add salary strings using floating-point arithmetic or silently change approved historical totals.

The after rows describe only committed outcomes. A rollback preserves the before financial rows; a separately committed failure/audit record can still describe the rejected request. Background document status changes do not rewrite the financial success.

paragraphs: Success means the defined financial operation and its associated local records are committed. Return the persisted reference and outcome to the client; do not generate a new success on each retry.
A successful response is sent after account/ledger/request writes commit together. If the response is lost, the next delivery reads the same committed success.

Insufficient funds is a confirmed business rejection: persist FAILED / INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS without a debit. An exception before COMMIT rolls back both debit and ledger. A deadlock victim may retry its database-only transaction; another client's completed withdrawal remains committed.

A repeated client delivery uses WD-CLIENT-001 and returns request 7001's SUCCESS. Retry a rolled-back database attempt only with the same request and bounded attempts. Do not create a fresh request merely because the HTTP response was lost.

paragraphs: Use bounded exponential backoff for transient technical errors and expose retry age/attempt count. An exhausted job becomes a failed/dead-letter item for an operator; a queue retry counter is not evidence of bank failure. A corrected obligation or authorized refund is a distinct linked business operation, not a stealth retry.

Callback authentication and idempotency solve different problems. Verify signatures/merchant context first; an attacker-controlled reference does not become trusted just because it is unique. Lock the request row before applying its result.

paragraphs: Laravel afterCommit() prevents a worker from reading an uncommitted row, but a process can still crash between database commit and sending to a separate queue. A transactional outbox closes that publication gap; consumers must still handle redelivery.

Separate payment, document, notification and reconciliation queues allow independent retries and limits. Payroll/corporate schedulers paginate or chunk work rather than loading all 10,000 payments into one transaction. Do not submit external payments again just because their notification jobs failed.

Each financial status change appends an audit event inside the same local transaction. Metadata includes the request ID, correlation ID, provider evidence reference and reason, with secrets and full beneficiary details removed.

Restrict update/delete permissions on audit history and define retention. A manual reconciliation resolution records the authorized operator, evidence and correction reference. Audit explains who changed a value; the ledger explains the financial entries.

items: Could the ₹10,000 request win the race?
It may acquire the lock first but still fails: the starting balance is only ₹5,000.
Why lock the request as well as the account?
The request lock serializes duplicate deliveries; the account lock serializes distinct debits sharing one balance.
Why SELECT FOR UPDATE?
Protect a mutable row while the transaction makes and applies a decision from its current value.
What does a waiting request read?
The new committed value after obtaining its lock, not a cached value from before waiting.
Why cannot local rollback reverse a bank payment?
The bank is outside the local transaction boundary; use verified reconciliation and a separate authorized reversal/refund.
How are duplicate webhooks prevented from repeating money effects?
Authenticate the event, persist unique provider/business keys, lock the saved payment and apply the final result once.
What distinguishes FAILED, PENDING and UNKNOWN?
Confirmed rejection; confirmed work in progress; and unresolved external outcome, respectively.
How do 5,000 student payments or 10,000 salaries scale?
Persist independent obligations, use controlled idempotent workers, avoid long global locks, and reconcile each result.
Why queue receipt generation?
Document availability can retry independently without changing a confirmed financial outcome.
What should a deadlock retry repeat?
The entire rolled-back local transaction with its original business identity; never an uncertain external payment.
